newsitem.title: USA: Colorado governor says missing now accounted for.
newsitem.headline: Colorado governor says missing now accounted for.

text.p: The death toll from a devastating flood in this college town remained at five on Wednesday, but all people who were missing have been accounted for, Colorado Gov. Roy Romer said.

"I'm informed that the death toll is five -- that all unaccounted persons have now been accounted for which really, really is good news," Romer told reporters at the site of a trailer park that suffered devastating damage.
On Tuesday, Romer, a Democrat, rushed from a governors' meeting in Las Vegas to view the devastation.
He said $4.5 million in state funds will be added to a $500,000 disaster fund.
"It will make a total of $5 million that will be available to begin to reconstruct and rehabilitate as of today," Romer said.
He said he also wrote President Clinton, seeking to have the area designated as a federal disaster area.
"The federal designation will make some loans and grants available. It's really crucial," he said.
The flash flood swept over Fort Collins Monday, also causing extensive damage to Colorado State University.
